hook: Arkansas sues VGW, Kalshi over *$66M* in bets
dek: Arkansas's AG hit two gambling platforms with lawsuits in one day.

slides.label: What Happened
slides.text: Arkansas AG Tim Griffin filed lawsuits against *VGW* and *Kalshi* on the same day, alleging illegal gambling.

slides.label: The Players
slides.text: VGW runs Chumba Casino, LuckyLand Slots and Global Poker, all built on the *Gold Coin/Sweeps Coin* model.

slides.label: The Numbers
slides.text: VGW reported *$66 million* in taxable Arkansas sales and paid $6 million in tax, but holds no state casino license.

slides.label: Age Concerns
slides.text: The suit claims VGW let *18 year olds* play, even though Arkansas casinos require players to be 21.

slides.label: Kalshi's Angle
slides.text: Kalshi is accused of taking sports wagers as unlicensed casino gaming, with no Arkansas authorization at all.

slides.label: Legal Claims
slides.text: Both suits cite the *Deceptive Trade Practices Act* and unjust enrichment, seeking restitution, penalties and taxes.

slides.label: Bigger Pattern
slides.text: Arkansas joins *Kentucky, Florida and New York*, where VGW already settled for $8 million in September.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: Sweepstakes and prediction apps market hard to everyday players, so who holds a license affects real wallets.

The lawsuit also claims VGW let 18 year olds play sweepstakes games, even though Arkansas casinos require players to be 21. Meanwhile Kalshi is accused of running unlicensed sports wagering disguised as a prediction market.

This is part of a bigger wave. Arkansas now joins Kentucky, Florida and New York, who already settled with VGW for $8 million in September. ReadWrite reports the state wants restitution, penalties, back taxes and an injunction.

Attorney General Tim Griffin filed lawsuits against VGW and Kalshi on the same day.
